properties.decision:
Recorded as brainstorming, not as a proposal. Nothing here is chosen.

THE OBSERVATION. `REALIZES` is `from: Artifact, to: "*"`. `IMPLEMENTS` is `from: Artifact, to: Verification`, enumerated deliberately, and the note beside it says why: "a wildcard would ACCEPT this pair and never MODEL it, so describe_schema would go on ranking it merely tolerated." On 2026-09-22 that prediction came true from the other side — `link_artifact` drew REALIZES onto Verifications for months, nothing refused it, and 47 checks carried an edge the schema's own hint calls wrong. The tool was fixed at the call site. The wildcard that allowed it was not.

THE OPTIONS, with what is cheap or expensive about each:

A. LEAVE IT. The wildcard is doing real work — measured on this design the same day, REALIZES points at Capability 401, Component 115, ChangeEvent 29, Requirement 7, Interface 1, TemporalFact 2. Six types, and at least three of those (ChangeEvent, TemporalFact) are uses nobody sat down and modelled. Cheap; leaves the next wrong pair equally writable.

B. ENUMERATE IT to the types it is actually used for. Turns "accepted" into "modelled" for six pairs and refuses the seventh. Expensive in a way that is easy to underestimate: it would refuse writes that work today, and the 38 REALIZES edges onto ChangeEvent/TemporalFact/Requirement have to be judged one at a time first — are they right, or are they three more instances of the same defect wearing different clothes? That question is the real work, and it is not answered.

C. EXCLUDE ONLY WHAT ANOTHER EDGE MODELS. A wildcard minus the pairs some enumerated edge already claims — so REALIZES would refuse Verification precisely because IMPLEMENTS names it. Says exactly the right thing and costs a schema feature that does not exist.

WHAT WOULD DECIDE IT: whether the 38 non-obvious REALIZES edges are correct. If most are, the wildcard is earning its keep and A is right. If most are the same defect, B pays for itself. Nobody has looked.

THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT TO DOING ANYTHING, and it is not weak: the measured defect had ONE cause reachable at ONE call site, and it is fixed and pinned. Narrowing a schema to prevent a class nobody has otherwise hit is the over-engineering Anthony names — engineers over-designing by nature, when a simple solution would do.
properties.name: SETTLED — promoted into: REALIZES may point only at a Capability, a Component or an Interface; the 37 edges that pointed elsewhere are repaired to the edge each should have been
properties.rationale: Raised while fixing `link_artifact` (chg:2026-09-22-link-artifact-draws-implements-for-a-check). The fix corrects the tool; this asks whether the schema should have made the mistake impossible. Recorded rather than acted on because the question underneath it — are the other 38 wildcard uses right? — is unmeasured, and narrowing a schema on an unmeasured hunch is the more expensive mistake.
